description:
Antarjatiye Vivah Protsahan Anudan Yojana is a significant welfare scheme initiated by the Government of India. 

This scheme was launched in 2013. 

It aims to promote inter-caste marriages in India. 

The initiative is a response to the social stigma and discrimination faced by couples who choose to marry outside their caste. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to encourage social harmony and integration. 

The government seeks to reduce caste-based discrimination through financial incentives. 

The scheme provides monetary assistance to couples who marry outside their caste. 

The financial assistance under this scheme is set at ₹2.5 lakh. 

This amount is provided to the couple as a one-time grant. 

The scheme is particularly aimed at couples where one partner belongs to a Scheduled Caste. 

This is to encourage individuals from marginalized communities to marry outside their caste. 

The financial assistance is intended to help the couple start their new life together. 

The scheme also aims to promote the idea of equality among different castes. 

To be eligible for the benefits of this scheme, certain criteria must be met. 

Both partners must be adults at the time of marriage. 

The minimum age for marriage is 21 years for males and 18 years for females. 

One partner must belong to a Scheduled Caste. 

The couple must provide proof of their marriage. 

This proof can be in the form of a marriage certificate issued by the relevant authorities. 

Additionally, the couple must not have received any other government assistance for the same purpose. 

The application process for the Antarjatiye Vivah Protsahan Anudan Yojana is straightforward. 

Couples must fill out an application form. 

This form can typically be obtained from the local government office or online portals. 

Along with the application form, several documents are required. 

These documents include identity proof for both partners. 

Proof of caste for the partner belonging to the Scheduled Caste is also necessary. 

A copy of the marriage certificate must be submitted. 

Additionally, proof of residence may be required. 

Once the application is complete, it must be submitted to the relevant government authority. 

This is usually the District Social Welfare Office or a similar department. 

After submission, the application will be reviewed by the authorities. 

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed to the couple's bank account. 

The disbursement typically occurs within a few weeks of approval. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

This ministry is responsible for overseeing the welfare of marginalized communities in India. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote social justice. 

The government has allocated a significant budget for this scheme. 

In recent years, the allocation has been around ₹100 crore annually. 

This funding is aimed at supporting couples who take the brave step of inter-caste marriage. 

The scheme has seen a positive response from the public. 

Many couples have benefited from the financial assistance provided. 

The government has reported an increase in inter-caste marriages since the launch of the scheme. 

This indicates a shift in societal attitudes towards caste-based marriages. 

The scheme also aims to create awareness about the importance of social integration. 

Workshops and campaigns are often organized to promote the benefits of inter-caste marriages. 

These initiatives are designed to educate the public about the negative impacts of caste discrimination. 

The government encourages local NGOs to participate in these awareness programs. 

This helps to reach a wider audience and promote the scheme effectively. 

The success of the scheme can be measured by the number of applications received. 

In the first year alone, over 10,000 applications were submitted. 

The number has steadily increased each year. 

This indicates growing acceptance of inter-caste marriages in society. 

The scheme also plays a role in empowering women. 

By encouraging women to marry outside their caste, it promotes their independence. 

Women are often the most affected by caste discrimination. 

The financial assistance helps them start a new life with dignity. 

The government has also set up a helpline for couples seeking assistance. 

This helpline provides information about the application process and eligibility criteria. 

It also offers guidance to couples facing challenges due to their inter-caste marriage. 

The scheme is a crucial step towards achieving social equality in India. 

It addresses deep-rooted issues related to caste and discrimination. 

The government continues to monitor the scheme's progress. 

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate its impact on society. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is also collected to improve the scheme. 

The Antarjatiye Vivah Protsahan Anudan Yojana represents a significant effort by the Indian government. 

It aims to foster a more inclusive and equitable society. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to social justice. 

It encourages individuals to rise above caste barriers and embrace love and unity. 

Overall, the Antarjatiye Vivah Protsahan Anudan Yojana is a vital initiative. 

It not only provides financial support but also promotes a cultural shift towards acceptance. 

The scheme is a beacon of hope for many couples in India. 

It stands as a reminder of the importance of equality and social harmony. 

The government continues to advocate for the rights of marginalized communities. 

Through this scheme, it aims to create a society free from caste-based discrimination. 

The future of the scheme looks promising as more couples come forward to benefit from it. 

It is an essential part of India's journey towards social reform. 

The impact of this scheme will likely resonate for generations to come. 

The government remains dedicated to ensuring its success and sustainability. 

The Antarjatiye Vivah Protsahan Anudan Yojana is more than just a financial scheme. 

It is a movement towards a more inclusive and equitable society in India.
